translation_notes: not-expressible: `g.query(sparql_get_all_properties, initNs=prefixes)` -- `prefixes` is the enclosing function's OWN parameter, a dict populated at runtime by the real caller (create_sql_checks_from_shacl.py:main) by parsing an external JSON-LD context file chosen on the command line (`context_graph.parse(context, format="json-ld"); for prefix, namespace in context_graph.namespaces(): prefixes[prefix] = rdflib.Namespace(namespace)`). `@prefix` takes a literal IRI known when the file is transpiled; confirmed with the transpiler that `@prefix ex: <{iri}> .` is a SyntaxError, same check as the GPViz.__init__ precedent elsewhere in this stratum. `sh:`, `rdfs:` and `rdf:` happen to be pre-bound by rdflib's own default NamespaceManager regardless of `initNs` (checked empirically: `Graph().query(q)` resolves `sh:NodeShape`/`rdfs:subClassOf`/`rdf:rest` with no initNs at all), but `ngsi-ld:` is not, and the query's FILTER clause (`?valuepath = ngsi-ld:hasValue || ...`) genuinely needs it -- dropping `initNs=prefixes` makes the query raise 'Unknown namespace prefix : ngsi-ld', checked directly (see the anti-hollow-green note below). Unlike GPViz.__init__, the query TEXT itself (`sparql_get_all_properties`) is a module-level literal, not a parameter -- only the namespace mapping is dynamic -- but that is exactly the part `@prefix` cannot stand for, so the outcome is the same: no island form here more specific than plain rdflib.
